{{Short description|French mathematician (1842–1906)}}
'''Gaston Albert Gohierre de Longchamps''' (1 March 1842 – 9 July 1906) was a French mathematician.<ref name="pdm">{{citation|title=Gastone Gohierre de Longchamps|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SHRVAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA53|pages=53–59|first=G.|last=Lazzeri|language=Italian|journal=Periodico di Matematica per l'Iinsegnamento Secondario|series=Ser. III|volume=4|year=1907}}.</ref>

Gohierre de Longchamps was born on 1 March 1842 in [[Alençon]]. He studied at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] beginning in 1863, and began a career as a teacher beginning in 1866. He retired from the [[Lycée Saint-Louis]], his final teaching position, in 1897, and died in [[Paris]] on 9 July 1906.<ref name="pdm"/><ref name="ayme">{{citation|title=Gaston Albert Gohierre de Longchamps dans les journaux scientifiques|first=Jean-Louis|last=Ayme|url=http://jl.ayme.pagesperso-orange.fr/Docs/Transversale%20reciproque.pdf|language=French|access-date=2012-09-06}}.</ref>

De Longchamps was a member of many international scientific societies, and in 1892 became a chevalier of the [[Legion of Honor]].<ref name="pdm"/> He was the editor of the ''Journal de mathématiques élémentaires'' and an associated journal, the ''Journal de mathématiques spéciales'', taking both journals over from their founder J. Bourget.<ref name="pdm"/><ref name="ayme"/><ref>{{citation|title=College Geometry: An Introduction to the Modern Geometry of the Triangle and the Circle|first=Nathan|last=Altshiller-Court|edition=2nd|publisher=Courier Dover Publications|year=2007|isbn=9780486458052|page=295|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VXDWIOvqeaoC&pg=PA295}}.</ref> The [[de Longchamps point]] of a [[triangle]] is named after him, for his 1886 study that identified this point.<ref name="ayme"/><ref>{{citation
 | last = Vandeghen | first = A.
 | doi = 10.2307/2311750
 | issue = 2
 | journal = The American Mathematical Monthly
 | mr = 1532529
 | pages = 176–179
 | title = Mathematical Notes: Soddy's Circles and the De Longchamps Point of a Triangle
 | volume = 71
 | year = 1964| jstor = 2311750
 }}.</ref>
